environment.note: Refresh executed in a local, non-shared Lima/QEMU x86-64 VM (souc-linux) on the operator's own machine, not the shared workspace pod or a Slurm node; slurm_partition/slurm_time above are the script's unused local-locked-path defaults, not evidence of a Slurm run. Staged via a minimal git snapshot (commit e4a20777d795 on this same branch name, containing only the files scripts/dev/refresh_lean_seed.sh needs) rather than a full checkout; git_commit/git_branch above have been corrected post-hoc to the real PR HEAD this source content was read from. source.sha256/md5/bytes were updated post-hoc after two further comment-only commits (thread 4116322276 fix's doc comment, then thread 4116544363's stale-NULL comment fix) changed lean_single.sio's bytes without changing its compiled output -- reconfirmed by recompiling with the unchanged seed ELF below and diffing md5 (unchanged) before each of those two commits landed. The seed/generations/fixed_point fields below describe the ELF, which did not need to change; only the source hash needed to catch up to the tree. Correction: git_commit was left at the pre-comment-fixes parent (53864a5f4cdf84a2f2a155da5d9eea57c4bdaa83) when source.sha256 was updated in the prior commit -- that SHA's tree does NOT contain a lean_single.sio matching this receipt's source.sha256 (verified: it hashes to 69461c45...). git_commit is now e5cd2992e2d395eac497ae4403a84c3c6636ad0b, the actual parent commit whose tree contains the exact source bytes source.sha256 describes (verified: git show e5cd2992e:self-hosted/compiler/lean_single.sio | sha256sum == c93151f9...), matching this repo's established convention of git_commit = the commit that precedes and contains the recorded source state (see 35513cf80, dcc9c12a7: both record their own parent SHA, not a self-referential pointer to the seed-refresh commit itself, which cannot be known before that commit exists).

limits.provenance_note: This receipt proves the installed ELF is a self-reproducing fixed point of the recorded source bytes (g_k == g_{k+1}, self-repro). It does NOT by itself prove the ELF was *derived from* that source rather than substituted from another generation that happens to self-reproduce the same source. canonical_compiler_gate.sh checks md5(committed)==md5(self-compile) — stability, not provenance. Provenance (ELF came FROM this source via this chain) is what the generation table + input_seed hashes are for; a future gate should require a SeedReceipt, not only the self-repro equality.
